statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (Guichet unique INPI) - formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Article R.123-6 of the Code de commerce, the corporate name must be written in Latin letters. Non-French names require a French transliteration or an acceptable Latin-character rendering. The name must not be contrary to public policy or liable to mislead third parties as to the object or legal form of the company. If a non-Latin script is used in branding, a Latin-character registered name must be filed in the RCS and used for official court and registry formalities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name refused by the Greffe or blocked by the Guichet unique is communicated in writing to the founder. The founder may resubmit the nomination through the same portal within 15 days with revised wording. If the registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may file an administrative request for reconsideration with the INPI Guichet unique within 15 days, and thereafter petition the president of the competent Tribunal judiciaire or Tribunal de commerce on an urgent motion under simplified proceedings where the registrar's decision is alleged to be arbitrary. No extension of the initial 30-day reservation is generally available; a new filing is required. A trademark-related conflict is appealed separately through Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle opposition proceedings under Articles L.712-4 et seq. of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or domiciliation office is acceptable for the statutory registered office of an engineering, design, and EPC administration SARL, provided a professional domiciliation agreement is made with an approved domiciliary agent in compliance with Article L.123-10-1 of the Code de commerce. The virtual office cannot operate as a sham; actual project management for reverse osmosis water treatment works will be performed at project sites, administrative centers, and authorized client facilities. The registered office must be able to receive official notices, process courier deliveries, and maintain statutory books.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: 5-10% annual probability for a clean virtual-office-only administrative seat holding no physical assets. This rises materially to 15-30% during active construction or commissioning phases at municipal sewage or water treatment sites, because the DREAL, the water police, and French labor inspectorate conduct unannounced site visits under the Environmental Code and Labour Code; such inspections target permits, personnel records, and site safety compliance rather than the registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), operating through the impots.gouv.fr portal; customs and export verification through Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI); corporate and VAT registration coordinated via the Réseau des Urssaf / Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a French SARL must file the statutory incorporation dossier with the CFE (now Guichet Unique) to obtain SIREN/SIRET numbers. VAT identification is issued automatically by DGFIP once the entity is registered; a non-established foreign entity may obtain a French intra-community VAT number by appointing a tax representative approved by DGFIP and filing the French VAT registration form (Form 3527-SD). For an existing SARL executing an ISIC 4220 EPC project, the company must ensure its SIRET and TVA intracommunautaire are active and, if intra-community acquisitions exceed €10,000 in a calendar year, file the EC Sales List and recapitulative statement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SARL is a separate French tax resident corporation subject to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés) on its worldwide profits; the territoriality principle applies, so certain foreign-source revenue may be excluded. A SARL that opts for the micro-company regime is not eligible; although a small SARL may be taxed at the reduced 15% corporate rate under statutory limits, ordinary income remains entity-level taxable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a check-the-box classification system. Elections available include (i) the option for the SARL to be treated as a partnership (option pour l'impôt sur les sociétés individuals cannot reverse to transparent; conversely, a société de personnes may elect corporate taxation) but for a SARL the default is corporate, (ii) the option to join a fiscal integration group under Articles 223 A to 223 T of the CGI if the parent holds at least 95% of the SARL, (iii) the VAT option for a single tax group under Article 256 C bis of the CGI, and (iv) the option for the reduced 15% corporate rate on the first €42,000 of taxable profits subject to strict conditions. Hybrid mismatch elections are regulated under Article 212 bis CGI and do not confer elective US-style check-the-box relief.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For established French businesses there is no statutory VAT registration threshold: every person carrying out a taxable economic activity in France must register for VAT. Non-established foreign businesses must register from the first taxable transaction, unless they qualify for the distance-selling threshold. For intra-community acquisitions of goods by a non-taxable person the registration threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year; for taxable persons, no threshold applies. For a reverse-charge/cross-border service provider, the customer's VAT registration generally triggers the obligation through a reverse-charge mechanism.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing is rolling out under the 2020 Finance Act: from 1 September 2026 all large and medium-sized entities must issue e-invoices and report transaction data through the Chorus Pro public portal or a certified Partner Dematerialisation Platform (PDP); all other taxable persons, including SMEs, must comply from 1 September 2027. E-reporting of payment data and cross-border supplies is mandatory. The system requires structured electronic invoices using EN16931-compliant formats (Factur-X, EDI or PEPPOL), with digital fiscal clearance through real-time validation by DGFIP. Tax clearance/fiscal stamping is not applied, but the transmission of each invoice to the Chorus Pro system or a certified PDP establishes the legal and fiscal timestamp. B2C and export invoices remain subject to standard archiving obligations and must be transmitted for e-reporting, not e-invoicing, under current rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under French VAT is available for (i) goods physically exported outside the European Union, provided the seller is a taxable dealer, the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU by or on behalf of the seller, and the buyer is not liable for VAT in France; zero-rating also applies to the supply of goods installed offshore or to EU customers in certain contexts under Article 258 and Article 262 of the French General Tax Code. For services, zero-rating (exemption with credit) may apply to services directly related to the export of goods, to cross-border transport, and to certain services rendered on movable property temporarily exported; for municipal sewage treatment works, French VAT at 20% generally applies to construction and installation services performed on French territory, but the supply of equipment to be exported is zero-rated if proof of export is retained. The contractual foreign-aid/World Bank or escrow payment does not per se create export status; the actual removal of goods or delivery of offshore services evidenced by transport documents is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane / ECS - Export Control System) lodged electronically via DELTA or NCTS
Commercial Invoice reflecting the terms, parties, and Harmonized System classifications
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure from EU territory
Shipping/transport proof and certificate of origin (EUR.1 or A.TR where applicable)
Proof of receipt by the foreign customer, including delivery acceptance certificate
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank documentation showing payment proceeds repatriated to the French entity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French customs and tax authorities (DGFIP and DGDDI) audit export files retrospectively. If the exporter cannot produce the complete export proof dossier within a period of at least three years from the return filing date, the zero-rating is denied and VAT is retroactively assessed. The standard late-payment interest at 0.20% per month applies, and a 40% penalty (Article 1729 CGI) for intentional incorrect tax returns will attach; where documentary fraud is established, a 80% penalty for bad faith or fraud (Article 1729-a-1 CGI) and up to €45,000 fine plus imprisonment penalty can be imposed. Customs infractions may trigger discounting of the export registration and confiscation of the goods. In practice, the six-month foreign-exchange repatriation benchmark is contractual/ADB-clearing standard and not a French statutory deadline, but missing foreign receipts without valid commercial reason will trigger a transfer-pricing and tax-nexus audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France in its capacity as French balance-of-payments, monetary and financial-stability authority, with prudential supervision of credit institutions and payment institutions by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR); ECB retains external monetary competence for the euro; DG Trésor retains international financial policy functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full de jure and de facto convertibility for the euro across both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange control permits, quotas, or ad hoc approval gates for ordinary inward/outward payments or profit repatriation. Capital movements between France and non-EU jurisdictions are liberalized under Articles 63-66 TFEU and the EU Capital Movements Directive, subject only to balance-of-payments statistical reporting to Banque de France, national security screening in exceptional circumstances, and tax treaty withholding mechanics. Profit remittances by a French SARL require corporate approval, audited accounts, and compliance with article L.227-? of the Code de commerce provisions on dividend distributions, but no FX authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios. Export receipts earned in foreign currency may be retained on account, converted freely, or used for foreign-currency disbursements. Banque de France requires periodic balance-of-payments reporting for aggregated cross-border flows and positions, but imposes no repatriation deadline, no conversion percent, and no obligation to deposit proceeds with any designated bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a principal treasury rail; Medium as an ancillary payment channel. A non-EU or offshore digital EMI without an EU/EEA banking or e-money licence and without ACPR registration or passport notification is legally prohibited from operating payment or deposit-taking services in France. An EEA-licensed EMI may provide limited cross-border payment initiation and collection services after ACPR passport notification, but French banks and public-sector escrow counterparties will not accept such an EMI for high-value capital escrow, World Bank-backed receivables, or SWIFT-based settlement. Required legal constraint: the EMI must hold a valid e-money or payment institution licence within the EEA, complete the freedom-to-provide-services filing with ACPR, and maintain a physical place of business or bundled programme without accessing the SARL's segregated clients account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banking institutions generally require physical identity verification of the legal representative, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners, or a video-identification process accredited to the French national e-identity standard (ANSSI-PVID) performed by the bank. Remote account opening is permitted for standard corporate structures using certified corporate documents combined with video interview; however, for SARLs with non-French shareholders or complex international ownership, banks routinely mandate a physical or notarial identification meeting, apostilled board resolutions, originals of the CEO signature card, and an in-person interview with the executive officer or an individually authorized mandataire. The KYC interview will validate source of wealth, source of funds, business purpose, and expected transaction patterns. For the stated municipal sewage treatment EPC scope, an additional face-to-face interview should be expected due to export-credit and public-project involvement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chain involving non-EU intermediate holdings, foreign trusts, or foundations above the 25% UBO threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized corporate organizational chart; 12-month-old excerpts from foreign business registries; UBO registry statement of the French entity; statutory auditor affidavit confirming ultimate beneficial ownership; board resolution listing transferors and the capital injection mechanism; reference letters from two ACPR-regulated lending institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or high-risk country exposure in the supplier/receiver network or shareholder base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions screening dashboard produced by the bank's correspondent; live OFAC, EU and UN sanctions registries; tax residence certificates of counterparties; full commercial rationale for each exposed jurisdiction; supply-chain export compliance certificates; evidence of no nexus to restricted industries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the company's stated municipal sewage treatment EPC activity and large cross-border payments to equipment vendors, consultants, or subcontractors outside the EU.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed EPC contract; World Bank or multilateral escrow agreement; itemized invoices and pro forma purchase orders; freight and customs declarations (SAD); insurance certificates; contractual delivery milestones; bank compliance approval with a cleared vendor whitelist; internal procurement policy reflecting the clearing-rail routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status, adverse media, or unexplained high-wealth profiles among directors or shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed CV and economic-purpose narrative; PEP status declaration with family-relationship chart; third-party corporate intelligence report from a licensed database; French criminal record extract (bulletin nº2) or the relevant foreign equivalent; professional reference letters from regulated corporate service providers; 24-month bank statements where applicable proving lawful source of funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The inbound capital injection must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or the ISO 20022 equivalent from the subscribing shareholder's account to the French SARL's designated operational account. The remittance instruction must include the mandatory ISO 20022 purpose code for equity capital contribution, commonly 'EQUI' or 'CAPT', and the beneficiary account must reference the SARL's SIREN identification and corporate name. For French balance-of-payments statistical purposes, the payment should be documented with the contributing shareholder, transaction nature, capital increase resolution, and confirmation of contribution without personal goodwill. Banque de France may require that the receiving bank file the flow under the French BOP declaration if the monthly aggregated threshold is crossed. The commercial bank will verify the debiting account ownership, corroborate the purpose with the underlying share subscription agreement and legalized board resolution, and may require a capital duty certificate or legal exemption letter before funds are credited without restriction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for equipment procurement, subcontractor payments, and EPC chain settlements should be made through SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for non-euro cross-border transactions or SEPA Credit Transfers for euro payments within the SEPA zone. For sovereign and multilateral project disbursements, the use of documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600 is advised, with the French confirming bank receiving SWIFT MT700/MT710 messages. Large-value disbursements may additionally require structured codes covering the underlying invoice, contract milestone, commodity classification, and shipping documents. The clearing rails are designed to ensure audit-ready reconciliation between the escrowed project funds, delivery milestones, and the approved supplier voice.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable foreign-exchange forwards (change à terme) entered into with an ACPR-regulated French or EU bank under an FBF/ISDA master agreement
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY swaps) for matched capex disbursements and long-term EPC debt-service hedging
Vanilla foreign-exchange options and zero-cost collars with a documented underlying transaction exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or restricted emerging-market currencies used in subcontracted procurement, subject to internal board risk limits

L.223-27 C. com.); repeated failure exposes the gérant to disqualification and damages claims.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and statutory tax package (liasse fiscale: nos. 2065-SD, 2050-2059 series incl. balance sheet, P&L and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP - Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (mandatory e-filing via EDI/EFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31-December accounting period: 3 May of the following year (extended to the 2nd business day after 1 May for e-filers); off-calendar periods: within 3 months of the fiscal-year close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% automatic late-filing surcharge (40% if filed over 30 days after formal notice) plus 0.20% monthly late interest under CGI arts. 1728 and 1731; underestimation of revenue for the reverse-osmosis EPC contracts triggers reassessment with the 40% deliberate-misconduct penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of approved annual accounts with management report, statutory auditor's report (if triggered) and RBE confirmation (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce via the Registre National des Entreprises (INPI electronic platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal-year close and in all cases within 1 month of the AGO approval (calendar-year SARL: filing due by 30 June unless a court order postpones the AGO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial court injunction with daily penalty (astreinte) under art. L.611-16 C. com.; late-filing administrative fine; non-deposit for 3 consecutive years permits judicial dissolution under art. L.613-2 C. com.; a Kbis extract without deposited accounts blocks qualification dossiers for municipal water/sewage tenders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE): update or confirmation of ultimate shareholders after any transfer or repayment of share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI RNE single digital register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in direct/indirect control or crossing a 10% ownership step; annual reconciliation performed at the accounts-deposit filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of up to EUR 7,500 for the gérant and EUR 37,500 for the SARL (CMF art. L.561-6); the registry blocks subsequent corporate filings until the RBE is regularised.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE): annual business property contribution (no separate return where the SARL already files under the real régime)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP - local tax office (paid at impots.gouv.fr)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment by 15 December of the assessment year (assessment notice issued August-September); initial activity declaration no. 1447-C due within 3 months of opening the water-treatment-plant site
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% automatic increase plus 0.20% monthly late interest (CGI art. 1731); enforced recovery by the tax collector without suspension of the obligation; personal liability of the gérant for intentionally withheld CFE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statement to tax authorities of sums paid to individuals and foreign beneficiaries (IFU no. 2561): dividends, interest on World Bank escrow accounts, fees to international subcontractors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 2nd business day after 15 February of the following year (art. 242 ter CGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: EUR 150 fine per omitted or incorrect statement capped at EUR 10,000 (CGI art. 1736); absence of documentation may re-characterise payments to affiliated EPC subcontractors as constructive dividends taxed at 30% PFU.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) becomes mandatory when the SARL exceeds at least two of the three following thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years - balance-sheet total EUR 4,000,000; net turnover EUR 8,000,000; 50 average employees (décret n°2019-514, applied at consolidated level where the SARL controls or is controlled by another entity); for a municipal sewage EPC company the trigger usually arises from balance-sheet assets on construction contracts or headcount peaks.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP - Plan Comptable Général (ANC règlement n°2014-03); IFRS applies only to listed consolidated accounts; long-term reverse-osmosis and sewage works must be recognised under the percentage-of-completion (à l'avancement) or completed-contract (à l'achèvement) method consistent with ANC title V and the bill-and-hold rules applicable to EPC retentions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law imposes a standing obligation to keep the beneficial-owner file permanently exact (CMF art. L.561-46); there is no standalone annual UBO return, but the RNE and the tax administration cross-check the RBE at each annual accounts deposit and each share transfer. Any transfer of registered shares or voting rights crossing a 10% step must be declared within 30 days of the deed, the register of members updated and the RBE re-filed; the company secretary integrates this check into the AGO preparation calendar and the statutory auditor (where appointed) verifies consistency between the register of members, the share-transfer deeds and the deposited RBE.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of members and share transfers (registre des associés et des mouvements de titres)
Minutes of shareholder meetings and written resolutions (registre des décisions et procès-verbaux d'AGO)
Beneficial-owner register (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE)
Register of employees (registre unique du personnel) where site and engineering staff are employed
Share-certificate and lock-up ledger for capital increases in the EPC holding structure

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 65-430 (EUR 60-400) per annum - standard commercial domiciliation with mail forwarding and Kbis address services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,400-21,500 (EUR 5,000-20,000) depending on the number of project SPVs, WIP verification and consolidation requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first €48,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover ≤ €10 million; research tax credit (CIR) up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses; innovation tax credit (CII) for SMEs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and annexes 2065-SD, 2065-B, 2065-R; filed electronically via the official portal 'impots.gouv.fr' (EFI - Echange de Formulaires Informatisés).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the 3rd month following the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, deadline is March 31). For fiscal years ending between January 1 and March 31, deadline is the 15th of the 4th month.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (bénéfice net imposable) after deduction of all allowable expenses and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a French permanent establishment must report French-source income only; attach Form 2065-SD for branch accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (crédits d'impôt) such as CIR, CICE, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim treaty credits only if a TRC is provided; otherwise, no credit is allowed.
Depreciation must be computed on French GAAP basis; non-residents must maintain separate books for the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carryforward losses (déficits reportables) applied to current year income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from French PE can be carried forward indefinitely, but annual deduction is capped at €1 million plus 50% of excess profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax on distributed profits (précompte) if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, dividend withholding tax is reported separately on Form 2561.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of tax due if filed within 30 days of deadline; 40% if filed after 30 days; 80% if tax evasion is established. Daily surcharge of 0.5% per month on unpaid tax, plus interest at 0.2% per month.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under a tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must submit Form 5000 (or 5001 for EU/EEA) to the French tax authorities before the payment date. A valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the home country must be attached. The French paying entity must also file Form 2561 to report the distribution. If treaty rate is 0% (e.g., EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive), the payer may apply the exemption at source upon receipt of the TRC and a declaration of ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: Royalties 33.33%, Interest 30%. Treaty rates typically reduce to 0% for royalties and interest under EU Interest & Royalties Directive (if 25%+ ownership) or under bilateral treaties (e.g., US-France treaty: 0% royalties, 0% interest). Application requires TRC and Form 5000.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Master File and Local File required if group turnover or assets exceed €400 million; simplified documentation (Form 2257) required for all other entities with intercompany transactions exceeding €50,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the abuse of law doctrine (abus de droit) and substance-over-form principles. While no specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) exist, tax residency requires effective management and control in France. For treaty benefits, the beneficial ownership test and principal purpose test (PPT) under MLI apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, false invoicing, or concealment of assets in a foreign jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 80% of the evaded tax, plus interest at 0.2% per month. Criminal fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they have committed fraud or gross negligence. Civil restitution, travel bans, and up to 7 years imprisonment for aggravated tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a French SARL with no real economic activity, no employees, no office, solely to obtain tax treaty benefits or avoid tax in another jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and imposition of 40% penalty for lack of substance. The company may be dissolved by court order.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held jointly liable for the company's tax debts if they are found to have used the company as a sham. Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML controls, accepting cash payments above €1,000, or failing to report suspicious transactions to Tracfin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million for companies; criminal penalties for directors up to €375,000 and 5 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML breaches if they knowingly participated or failed to supervise. Travel bans and seizure of personal assets may occur.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for EPC services or equipment sales that deviate from arm's length, resulting in profit shifting out of France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, 40% penalty for lack of documentation, and interest. If deemed fraudulent, 80% penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation may face criminal charges for tax fraud, leading to imprisonment and personal fines.
